messages.author: edd4914c326b6d31
messages.subject: rstan memory use
parts:
A lot of the memory rstan's fit objects use is sneaking in through the
back door.

I have one fit object that is about 488Mb when saved to disk with
save(). The .Misc object (one of the slots), which is an environment,
occupies 435Mb of that. The environment itself has only one item, which
doesn't look too big. So I assume what is happening is that the
enclosing environment, and its enclosing environment, and so on are
getting saved as well.

My understanding is that environments are shared objects, so that
multiple objects referencing the same environment see the same thing,
and do not create copies. Also, at least some environments (maybe the
base and global environments) are not saved to disk. I'm not sure if
package environments (imports:rstan is toward the top of the enclosing
environment frames for .Misc) are saved, or simply an indication to load
the appropriate library (since I've noticed that load() can trigger
messages that libraries are being loaded).

My typical usage involves saving fit objects to disk and then reading
them into other processes. I suspect that this breaks the sharing of
environments, that is a I get one new copy with each object read in.

I don't know if there's anything that can be done about this, but if
there's a way to avoid it that would be nice.

I discovered this because I've been running simulations with multiple
fit objects, and my jobs require a lot of memory, like 16GB. I have
also been sending some objects between processes (with Rmpi).
environments crop up in a lot of unexpected (to me) places: every
formula has one, and so does a model frame. And so does a stanfit
object. So, for example, I have one formula that required 3.5G to save
to disk; it was a couple hundred bytes after I replaced the environment
with one of the canonical ones like emptyenv() or baseenv(). I later
discovered empytenv() was a poor choice since it causes operations on
the formula to fail with messages like "can't find list function".

Ross Boylan

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-dev] rstan memory use
parts:
What we really need is a format to save fits that portable
across CmdStan/RStan/PyStan and doesn't involve any R at all!
We're moving in that direction, and will hopefully work something
out at some point this year (not a very encouraging time frame,
but it is on our medium-term to-do list).

Having said that, I have no idea whether the environments are
there for a reason in R or not.

- Bob
